subject: Week 36: 9-month visit window opens Monday — first steps for some
bodyText:
This week
First-step territory opens for early walkers this week — the full range runs 9-17 months, and the CDC moved its walks-alone checkpoint to 15 months, so later is not a lag. Expect brief unsupported stands for some, functional object use (cup to mouth, phone to ear), and possibly a first specific word: mama or dada aimed at the right parent. The 9-month well-visit window opens Monday Jan 18.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Falls rise as cruising speeds up — the standard is supervised falls onto forgiving surfaces, not zero falls.
- [low concern] Everything still goes in the mouth — keep the daily floor sweep going.
- [monitor] Babble that stays vowel-only, without consonant variety — raise it at this month's visit.
- [call within 24h] Persistent illness that is not improving.
- [call now] Fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy; labored breathing or blue lips — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Practice walking his way: hold both hands and let him step, or set a weighted push toy along the cruising route. Keep him barefoot indoors — bare feet beat shoes for early balance; save soft soles for outdoor surfaces. AAP: Movement 8-12 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Decide the Suzuki question before the option lapses Feb 5: pick the instrument (violin, piano, or cello), start Book 1 recordings 30+ min/day, and join named-teacher waitlists — top SF teachers run multi-year lists, so listing now targets a 2029-2030 lesson start. Cost today: recordings only. Suzuki Association directory: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Play give-and-take: ask for the toy with an open hand, thank him, hand it back. Giving objects on request sits on the CDC 1-year checklist and doubles as turn-taking rehearsal. CDC 1-year milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Shift reading toward retrieval practice — name an image and let him find it on the page. Pointing on request is exactly what the ASQ-3 samples. Reach Out and Read: https://reachoutandread.org/

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — window opens Monday; iron rescreen, influenza #2 if first season, possible ASQ-3. Bring the notes file: babble variety, feeding, sleep, mobility.
- Day 270 (Feb 5, 2027): Suzuki teacher-waitlist and ISR instructor-contact windows both close — ISR decision detail next week.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Pulls to stand at furniture or your legs
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Time to switch to a lower crib mattress setting if not already.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pulls-to-stand/complete

- Babbles with inflection (sounds like speech)
  AAP window: day 240-330
  What to look for: Jargon. Pitch and rhythm of a sentence without recognizable words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/babbles-with-inflection/complete

- Explores objects by shaking, banging, throwing, dropping
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Systematic property exploration. Repetitive drops are research, not defiance.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/explores-objects-many-ways/complete

- Lets objects go voluntarily (drops on purpose)
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Controlled release — distinct from accidental dropping. Predecessor to throwing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/lets-objects-go-voluntarily/complete

- Pokes with index finger
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Isolated finger use. Predecessor to pointing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pokes-with-index/complete
